Try Kingyo Sukui — Japan's most iconic festival game!✨

At this cute specialty shop in Asakusa, you can enjoy it anytime!

📍 Asakusa Kingyo
・Located at the entrance of Sensoji's West Market Street
・Open 9:00–16:00
・400 yen per try

📝 What's special?
・Scoop goldfish using a tool made of washi (traditional Japanese paper) 
・It tears if soaked or moved too fast—trickier than it looks!!
・Traditional Hinoki wood tanks create a calm, Japanese vibe 🌿
・Lots of cute, goldfish-themed souvenirs too! 

Visiting Asakusa? Don't miss this spot!

transcription: This is Japan's most popular festival game, King Yosuke, in Asakusa. Just 400 yen for two paper scoops made of washi. Go slow and scoop it up. Don't tear the washi paper. The black ones are so fast. Cut for today. And look! So many cute goldfish themed souvenirs. Tokyo vibes right here. Follow me.

transcription: I got a lot of questions after posting about the Mount Fuji swing and the first one was, was it crowded? I visited in a Tuesday around 11.30am and no, it wasn't crowded at all. When I arrived, a couple was using this swing, but there was no line and no one was waiting after me. At the second swing, there was literally no one else around. Yes, there are actually two swings. This pod also offers plenty of fun activities like cow milking, horseback riding, and feeding or petting the farm animals perfect for a day out. Another question I got was, is this in Kawaguchi-ko? No, it's actually in Shizuoka Prefecture and this place is called Makai no Farm.

Tokyo Overlooked - Nakano

Nakano is a must-visit gem in Tokyo, offering a mix of charm and pop culture energy. Explore narrow backstreets lined with local izakayas, music bars, and one or two livehouses. Then dive into the iconic Nakano Broadway—famous for its anime, manga, and collectible finds. It’s where Tokyo drinking culture meets otaku paradise, all in one stop.

Locations/Recommendations:
📍Nakano Broadway (For Everything Retro & Anime + Watches)

transcription: This is Tokyo's anime and drinking epicenter. Stop going akihabura if you want anime goods. Nakano's less crowded and features Nakano Broadway, selling anime and manga goods, use kimonos, Rolex watches, and even more. But next to Nakano Broadway is also a great cafe scene during the day. And I bet you didn't know that it turns into one of Tokyo's richest nightlife areas, with bars and izakaya in the middle of the street, and even live houses. Nakano is one of the best places for people into anime and of Tokyo culture. Despite Nakano Broadway losing a lot of local businesses to scalping in COVID, It's still an amazing market to buy from, and with an amazing nightlife. I can't recommend not going to enough, since it's right next to Shinjuku, it's a must visit for Japan trip. And for more Overlooks, Boston Japan, follow Tomogo.
